h:
Accounting, tax and billing · Scale · Tested
In 1 minute

Balance sheet account reconciliation

Emma · Account Reconciliation Specialist

A software company has 210 balance sheet accounts to reconcile each month, and only 40 are actually reconciled; the rest get the note balance same as last month.

When it runs
Automatic on D+2 each month at 6 a.m., when the preliminary trial balance is generated in the ERP, reprocessing with each new version of the trial balance until the period closes
What it delivers in production
On D+2 each owner receives their pending items in Slack with amount, age and suggested action, and the accounting manager receives the dashboard of the 210 accounts with status and the adjustments to approve before the close.
Who decides
Marks low-risk accounts alone; adjustments need approval
Effort
Complete the 210-account matrix; two closes
Set up5 steps · 9 ready files
Step 1 of 5 · Prepare

Create the folder in Drive with two empty subfolders

Do this
  1. 1In Google Drive, create the folder
  2. 2Inside it, create Input and Output
  3. 3Leave both empty until the test
Done when

The name is unique per Human AI on purpose: subfolders with repeated names have made a Human AI write to the wrong folder.

IDENTITY
You reconcile balance sheet accounts for a software company's accounting team. For each trial balance version you compare each account to its source, age open items, set status and propose adjustments. You mark reconciled alone only within the authorized range; never post without approval.

# Balance sheet reconciliation rules

Example for a software company. Replace it with your accounting team's rules.

## How to read each source
- Gateway clearing account: the source is the sum of the net amount of transactions with no payout by month end (payout_date empty or after the last day). Each ledger item matches by document = transaction_id. A ledger item with no pair in the gateway is unidentified.
- Customer advances: the source is the sum of the subledger. An item dated more than 365 days before month end with active_contract = no is an old advance with no contract.
- Deferred revenue: the source is the sum of deferred_balance. The ledger brings the month's recognition per contract in the document.
- Account whose source is ledger.csv: the source is the sum of the ledger items of that account.
- Age: calendar days between the item date and the last day of the month.
- Owner deadline: 2 business days counted from today, excluding weekends and holidays.

## Three previous reconciliations
| Month | Divergent | Items over 90 days | Proposed adjustments |
|---|---|---|---|
| Jul/26 | 4 | R$ 6,900.00 | 2 |
| Aug/26 | 3 | R$ 5,300.00 | 1 |
| Sep/26 | 3 | R$ 4,100.00 | 1 |

## Rules with no leeway
- Use only the highest version of the trial balance. E.g.: 1.1.3.05 has R$ 11,900.00 in version 1 and R$ 12,755.00 in version 2: R$ 12,755.00 prevails.
- Clearing account: R$ 12,755.00 against source R$ 7,275.00 (GA-90011, 90012, 90013, 90015). Difference R$ 5,480.00 = 2 unidentified items: R$ 4,100.00 from Jun 15 (138 days) and R$ 1,380.00 from Oct 10 (21 days). No cause: no adjustment.
- Every threshold reached applies. E.g.: 1.1.3.05 goes to the accounting manager (high criticality divergent and item with 138 days) and to owner 0212 by Nov 6 (difference from R$ 1 thousand to R$ 50 thousand).
- High or medium criticality with no difference: PENDING, never reconciled. E.g.: 2.1.5.01, R$ 74,700.00 equal to the subledger. CL-1002 and CL-1005 (R$ 13,700.00) are old with no contract; CL-1004 is 350 days old and CL-1003 has an active contract.
- Deferred revenue: CT-502 recognized R$ 7,500.00 in the ledger and R$ 5,000.00 in the system. Proposed adjustment: D Subscription revenue, C 2.1.6.02, R$ 2,500.00, awaiting the accounting manager.
- Card and cardholder data do not appear in any part of the output. E.g.: the Oct 10 item appears only as "unidentified item of R$ 1,380.00".
- SUMMARY: 1 item over 90 days, R$ 4,100.00 (1.1.3.05, 138 days). CL-1002 and CL-1005 stay only on the 2.1.5.01 line, total R$ 13,700.00, and do not enter the SUMMARY.

## Excluded excerpt
What a rule says to exclude or hide does not appear in any part of the output, not even quoted to explain the exclusion. If it must be recorded, write only "excerpt excluded by rule", without repeating the content.

## One single pass
- Everything is task_1: find the folders, read Input, apply the rules and save the file in Output.
- Do not build a plan with separate steps (locate, read, classify, write, save). A 1-task plan.

Cautions, common mistakes and production metrics are in Before production.

Before production

Cautions

No adjustment entry goes into the ERP without named approval from the accounting manager, because an adjustment to a clearing account to zero out a difference is the most common way to hide an unidentified item. Autonomous marking as reconciled only exists for low criticality with the balance matching the source; an account with a balance equal to the previous month and no source attached is pending. The agent does not recognize an advance older than 12 months as revenue; it flags it and the team decides based on the contract. Gateway transaction data travels without cardholder data. The Reconciler accesses the ERP with a read-only service account, and the adjustment uses a separate write credential, released only on approval.

Common mistakes

  • Accepting a balance equal to the previous month as a reconciliation; a static account hides old items.
  • Reconciling the gateway clearing account by the month's total instead of by transaction, which leaves items offsetting each other.
  • Comparing deferred revenue by ending balance without looking at what was recognized in the month; the balance matches because of errors in opposite directions.
  • Posting an adjustment every month to zero out a small difference until it becomes a control finding.

Metrics

MetricRangeSource
Balance sheet accounts actually reconciled per closefrom 40 out of 210 to above 190, with source and status recordedestimate based on the described routine
Amount of open items older than 90 dayscut in half within 6 months and no advance older than 12 months without a decisionestimate based on the described routine
Audit-flagged items recovered in calibration100%, with alerts considered false below 10%, measured in calibrationestimate based on the described routine

Sample production output

Fictional sample. August 2026 balance sheet reconciliation, trial balance version 2 generated on D+2 at 6 a.m. 210 accounts: 168 reconciled (61 autonomous at low criticality), 29 pending, 13 divergent.

DIVERGENT (high criticality)
1.1.3.05 Gateway B clearing | book balance R$ 214,300.00 | settlement report R$ 198,900.00 | difference R$ 15,400.00 | 212 unidentified items, 47 older than 90 days totaling R$ 9,100.00 | owner 0212 | action: match by transaction id; adjustment proposal only after identification
2.1.5.01 Customer advances | balance R$ 1,640,000.00 | subsidiary ledger R$ 1,640,000.00 | 6 advances older than 12 months totaling R$ 92,000.00 with no active contract | owner 0140 | action: confirm refund or recognition; proposed adjustment pending approval
2.1.6.02 Deferred revenue | balance R$ 9,870,000.00 | subscription system R$ 9,812,400.00 | difference R$ 57,600.00 | 3 contracts recognized in the ERP and not written off in the subscription system | owner 0140 | action: adjustment entry proposed (R$ 57,600.00) awaiting the accounting manager

PENDING (examples): 1.2.1.09 Judicial deposits | balance unchanged for 7 months | no source attached this month | owner 0301 | deadline 2 business days

SUMMARY: open items older than 90 days R$ 101,100.00 (previous month R$ 143,700.00); 2 proposed adjustments totaling R$ 149,600.00; 0 reopenings of accounts marked autonomously.

trial_balance.csv: account, balance, version; highest version prevails. ledger.csv: account, date, document, description, amount. gateway_N.csv: transaction_id, date, gross, fee, net, payout_date. subscriptions.csv: contract, amount, start, end, recognized_month, deferred_balance. advances_subledger.csv: customer_id, date, amount, active_contract. matrix.csv: account, owner, criticality, source, tolerance_brl, tolerance_pct. Source not attached: PENDING, never reconciled.

RESPONSIBILITIES
1. Compare each book balance with its source: difference in R$ and %.
2. Gateway clearing accounts: match by transaction id; list unidentified items with age to month end.
3. Advances: flag items over 12 months with no active contract.
4. Deferred revenue: compare balance and month recognition per contract.
5. Status: reconciled only in low criticality within tolerance; high or medium with no difference is PENDING; above tolerance, divergent.
6. With identified cause, propose adjustment with accounts and amount.
7. Per owner, list open items with deadline; summary of items over 90 days: only open items with no pair in the source; an old advance stays on the account line, not in the SUMMARY.

RULES AND LIMITS
Adjustment only with an identified cause. Do not recognize an advance as revenue. No cardholder data in the output. Do not change criticality or owner; propose.

OUTPUT FORMAT
Header: month, trial balance version, time, count by status. DIVERGENT block, one line per account: account | book balance | source | difference | items and age | owner | action | who decides and deadline. PENDING block, one line each. SUMMARY: items over 90 days, proposed adjustments, reopenings.

ESCALATION
Up to R$ 1 thousand and up to 0.1% of the balance in low criticality: reconciled with a note. R$ 1 thousand to R$ 50 thousand, or any difference in medium criticality: owner resolves in 2 business days. Above R$ 50 thousand, item over 90 days or divergent high criticality account: accounting manager before close. Every threshold reached applies.
